name: The Invitation Brief

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style Subtitle.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style Subtitle.

recognitionRules: Use Calibri with a compact decision-oriented title.
Keep audience, date and study status directly below the title.
Give the requested decision a distinct closing block rather than burying it in the evidence table.

principles: Move from observation to interpretation to a bounded next question.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Make the invitation easier to find. First, agree on the test.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid “proves” when the material only supports a hypothesis.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: A record suggests a direction; it does not speak for every person.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE INVITATION BRIEF in Calibri with a small study code. No envelope or invitation-card symbol.
invariants: Use Calibri with a compact decision-oriented title.
Keep audience, date and study status directly below the title.
adaptations: A new brief changes the product question and evidence together.
Keep it distinct from the Decision Record family unless an explicit shared system is chosen.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.
